description: Simulated 'today' at tick 0 (day 0, 00:00). The data dictionary states today = 2026-10-05.
Seed of the deterministic random numbers (noise, hourly spreading, delivery hours).
Real milliseconds per simulated hour while running (default 5 s).
Smallest allowed interval between ticks.
Speed presets shown in the top bar.
Pause the simulation when a critical event appears.
Upper limit for 'run N hours' / 'jump' actions.
Display offset of the warehouse (Oman, UTC+4, no DST). The clock itself is an integer tick.
Daily demand noise around the baseline (+/-).
History window (days before the last data day) used as the baseline usage.
Relative demand per hour of day 0-23 (heavier in working hours, light at night). Normalised automatically.
Seasonal items and their peak multiplier: ramps up from ramp_start over ramp_days, holds until season_end, then eases off over decay_days.
One-off demand events (spike factor, days held at full factor, days to ease off).
Baseline window for items with a demand event (the weeks before the spike).
Weeks compared in the anomaly test.
Reference weeks before the recent weeks.
Anomaly when recent weekly usage exceeds this multiple of the prior average.
Ignore anomalies on very small volumes.
Forecast horizon.
How far the stock-out projection looks.
Critical when cover is below this and no PO arrives soon.
A PO arriving within this many days softens 'Critical' to 'Low'.
Low when cover is below this (or stock below safety stock).
Overstock status / alert above this cover.
Expiry alert / status window.
Expiry alert becomes High inside this window.
Expiry alert becomes Critical inside this many hours (when stock would be written off).
Stock-out alert when projected within lead time + this many days.
Stock-out within this many days counts as imminent.
Item category treated as safety items.
Temporary substitute item per item, used in supplier messages.
Review cycle added to the lead time in the reorder point.
Never reorder above this cover.
Order quantity covers lead time + this many days.
For perishables the cover is limited to this share of the shelf life.
Round order quantities up to a multiple per unit.
Categories ranked first inside a criticality class (after stock-out risk).
A rejected PO draft is not proposed again before this many hours...
...unless cover has fallen below this share of the cover at rejection (materially worse).
Emergency POs use this share of the normal lead time (minimum 1 day).
Price premium on emergency purchase orders.
A recommendation left pending this long raises an 'overdue' alert.
Overdue becomes Critical when the stock-out is closer than this.
'Postpone' hides a recommendation for this many hours (it keeps ageing but no overdue alert is raised meanwhile).
How long the Undo button stays on the confirmation toast after a decision.
Zone that receives goods which do not fit in their home zone.
Storage type of requests that can be served from rentable zones.
Below this share of the request no partial offer is made.
Deliveries arrive from this hour...
...until this hour (exclusive). Each PO gets a deterministic hour inside the window.
Remainder of a partially received PO is retried after this many hours.
Lots are usable until the end of this hour on their expiry date; the rest is written off right after.
Hours at which the alert agent runs (cheap rules).
Hours at which the forecast agent runs.
Hours at which the replenishment agent runs.
Hours at which the space optimisation agent runs (also after stock-heavy events).
Older agent_runs rows are pruned.
Rows per page in the live feed and logs ('load more').
